title: 北京东胡林遗址植物遗存浮选结果及分析 (Plant remains unearthed at the Donghulin site in Beijing: discussion on results of flotation)
version: Kaogu (Archaeology) 2020 no. 7, pp. 99–106, Chinese original presented with the ResearchGate item for the 2021 English translation (DOI 10.1515/char-2021-0015).
lineage: Original report on charred remains from flotation. Several authors overlap with the Yang et al. starch study, but the specimens and analyses are distinct.

passages.note: Report of 14 charred specimens assigned morphologically to foxtail millet (Setaria italica), one assigned to broomcorn millet and 11 to green foxtail (Setaria viridis).

passages.locator: pp. 103–104, chronology and caution about displacement
passages.note: Four deposit units yielded the foxtail millet grains. Four pooled grains from one unit were too small for the attempted direct AMS date. A cork-tree seed from a deposit also containing charred foxtail millet was directly dated as BA07888, 8885 ± 55 radiocarbon years BP, calibrated to 8240–7820 BCE at 95.4%. This is a context date for one millet-bearing unit.
